MC	<p>d5b3_83b9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ejr, +++, ejr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a29e_60d9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpw, +++, fpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f623_4d8e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bct, +++, bct"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4a16_f911</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bht, +++, bht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>79f7_8575</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fwy, +++, fwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f0de_d1db</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnx, +++, bnx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, any, +++, any"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3440_0429</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ewy, +++, ewy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3aae_25f1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, frw, +++, frw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chj, +++, chj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1cf8_b1ee</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #186f3b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdh, +++, cdh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0df4_3c5d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekp, +++, ekp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhw, +++, bhw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>660f_5d19</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hxy, +++, hxy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dmp, +++, dmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>965d_51a0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jwx, +++, jwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fcae_cb06</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhr, +++, dhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ach, +++, ach"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ac6c_a111</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ceh, +++, ceh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehj, +++, ehj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, htw, +++, htw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>40a1_b083</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>88c7_fde5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bjk, +++, bjk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6b21_d203</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpy, +++, hpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6a18_d909</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehr, +++, ehr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7198_3ffe</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #186f3b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bwx, +++, bwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhk, +++, dhk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f55f_4b46</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #186f3b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cen, +++, cen"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2911_ed47</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpy, +++, mpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7b60_9ff5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>71ad_a824</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #186f3b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cey, +++, cey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>eee3_ccba</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jnt, +++, jnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e59;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e59;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e59;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>538c_acc5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bem, +++, bem"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c0c7_278f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amn, +++, amn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5f0f_8c0d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fjt, +++, fjt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3d42_9982</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aep, +++, aep"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ac52_7897</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aht, +++, aht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>dbdc_5045</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #544fb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544fb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfw, +++, cfw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5d35_7c0f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfj, +++, cfj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcy, +++, bcy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8e5b_cbe3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006b6d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863d84;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, npt, +++, npt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>01a7_aab6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #446b07;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #446b07;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b07;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehm, +++, ehm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
