MC	<p>4d88_bc2a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983e11;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983e11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7341a5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7341a5;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bpt, +++, bpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b19c_5565</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884e00;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #884e00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884e00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #186f3b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186f3b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863d84;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #863d84;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a42b35;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a42b35;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #646110;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646110;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646110;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #315ca5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315ca5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpx, +++, hpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>73b1_4321</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #765908;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #765908;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #765908;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006595;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006595;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9c2c64;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c2c64;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kpr, +++, kpr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
